references.text: The preceding verse provides the context for Zipporah circumcising her son and touching Moses' feet with the foreskin, which caused the Lord to let him go.
God's covenant with Abraham regarding circumcision as a sign of the covenant, which is the basis for why circumcision was so important and why Zipporah acted as she did.
Circumcision as a requirement to participate in the Passover meal, illustrating the significance of circumcision within Israel's covenant relationship with God.
The law requiring circumcision on the eighth day, emphasizing the importance of this ritual in Israel's faith.
The circumcision of the Israelites at Gilgal after they crossed the Jordan, where the expression 'rolled away the reproach of Egypt' highlights the cleansing function of blood and circumcision.
